newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end flat to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end flat to lower.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bonds' good start fizzled as prices ended flat to slightly lower, while in new issues, Houston's controller said an upcoming election hurt the city's $382 million bond offering.
Prices were firmer early in the session, but finished unchanged, a trader said.
"It's really quiet," the trader said, adding that players are eyeing Thursday's producer price index and Friday's employment data.
"The unemployment number is a huge number here," the trader said.

Economists polled by Reuters expect December producer prices to rise by 0.3 percent overall and by 0.1 percent excluding food and energy. December non-farm payrolls are expected to increase by 192,000.
A municipal analyst said dollar bonds were up 1/8 by noon EST but faded to end about 1/8 point lower. High-grades finished mostly unchanged, developing a slightly weaker tone near the close, he said.
In debt futures, the March municipal contract closed down 2/32 at 114-19/32. The March T-bond contract closed down 5/32 at 110-23/32. The MOB spread was 124 ticks.
In the government cash market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed down 20/32 at 95-21/32 to yield 6.84 percent.
As for new issues, an analyst described pricing on three big deals by PaineWebber in as "firm."
PaineWebber repriced Houston's $381.7 million water and sewer bond deal, lowering yields by five basis points in several maturities, but leaving the top yield in 2027 unchanged at 5.80 percent.

Despite the lowered yields, Houston City Controller Lloyd Kelley said a concern over a January 18 election that Moody's Investors Service said could "severely alter the city's revenue-raising ability," cost the city money on the offering. Overall, Kelley estimated that the city paid about four basis points too much in borrowing costs.

Also Wednesday, PaineWebber said it repriced $262.1 million Port of Oakland, Calif., bond deal, lowering yields in some maturities, and cutting the top yield in 2025 to 5.89 percent from 5.91 percent.

The firm also repriced the State Building Commission of West Virginia's $99.9 million lottery bond deal, lowering yields five basis points in several maturities, and cutting the top yield in 2010 to 5.50 percent from 5.55 percent.
